# Move control buttons for gym scenes to the bottom

## Problem statement

In gym scenes, the EXPLODE and SHOOT control buttons are positioned at the top-left of the screen (y=10), overlapping with the HUD info line and obscuring important game status information.

## Users

- **Game developers testing formations** — need clear visibility of the HUD while interacting with gym controls.
- **Players in combat gyms** — need to see their ship status, score, and power-up information without obstruction.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Buttons moved to bottom:** The EXPLODE and SHOOT buttons are repositioned to the bottom of the screen, clear of all HUD elements.
2. **AC2 — Status text follows:** The score/status text line moves to sit alongside the buttons at the bottom of the screen.
3. **AC3 — No visual regression:** Button styling (monospace neon style) and interactivity are preserved exactly.
4. **AC4 — Back button stays:** The "← INDEX" back button remains at the top-right corner.
5. **AC5 — Hint text stays:** The bottom hint text remains at its current position.
6. **AC6 — Tests pass:** All existing gym scene tests continue to pass; any button-position assertions are updated.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — test assertions:** Some gym scene tests may assert button y-positions or viewport bounds. These will need updating. Low risk; straightforward positional changes.
- **Risk — per-scene overrides:** If any concrete gym scene (GymEnemies, etc.) sets button positions independently, those must also be updated. (Checked: buttons are created in the base class.)
- **Assumption — bottom position:** Buttons will be placed at the bottom-left, just above the hint text line. The exact y-offset is left to implementation (e.g., `GAME_HEIGHT - 30`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** The GymEnemies.ts scene has its own set of `<button>` DOM elements (Respawn, Toggle Player, Save, Save As) in a separate panel. These are outside the canvas scope and are **not** part of this change. If those also need repositioning, that is a separate task.

## Constraints

- Changes are scoped to `GymFormationScene.ts` (the shared base class for all gym formation scenes).
- No new features or behavioural changes — only repositioning.
- Maintain consistency with the existing monospace neon button style.

## Existing state

- **EXPLODE button:** `_addButton(10, 10, 'EXPLODE', LABEL_STYLE)` at top-left.
- **SHOOT button:** `_addButton(120, 10, 'SHOOT: OFF', LABEL_STYLE)` at top-left.
- **Status text:** `add.text(10, 44, ...)` just below the buttons.
- **Back button:** `addBackToIndexButton(this)` at top-right (x=GAME_WIDTH-10, y=10).
- **Hint text:** `add.text(GAME_WIDTH / 2, GAME_HEIGHT - 12, ...)` at bottom-center.
- **Screen size:** 960×540.

## Desired change

Move the EXPLODE and SHOOT buttons and status text from the top-left to the bottom-left of the screen, keeping the same horizontal layout but shifting vertically to sit just above the hint text.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Reposition button creation in `create()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Update any button-position assertions.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

No clarifying questions were needed — the work item description was sufficiently detailed to draft a clear brief. The codebase confirmed the exact button positions and scene structure.

## Related work

- **Gym scene refactoring:** AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 (Extract reusable gym formation-scene core library)
- **Scheme-aware gym controls:** AH-0MTFRQR41000V57V
- **Gym editor panel:** AH-0MTHG5BIB006PP0P

# Boss dies in single hit instead of 4-phase health

## Problem statement

The Boss ("The Central AI", GDD §4.3) in `GymBoss` scene is destroyed immediately when a single player bullet hits it, instead of progressing through its 4-phase health bar as designed.

## Users

- **Developer** testing the Boss gym scene — expects the Boss to require 4 bullet hits to defeat, with phase transitions updating attack patterns and visuals.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need player-bullet collision to properly delegate to `Boss.takeDamage()` for correct phase progression.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer** testing the Boss gym scene, I want player bullets to damage the Boss through its 4 health phases so I can verify the health bar progression.
- As a **developer**, I want the Boss to change attack patterns after each hit so I can verify phase transitions.
- As a **developer**, I want the DAMAGE and EXPLODE buttons to continue working as before.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Player bullet hits decrement Boss health:** Each player bullet hit to the Boss decrements one health phase via `Boss.takeDamage()`. The Boss requires 4 hits to destroy.
- [ ] **AC2 — Phase transitions update attack pattern and visuals:** After each hit, the Boss's current phase advances, its attack pattern changes, and visual cues (core exposure, health bar color) update.
- [ ] **AC3 — DAMAGE button still works:** The existing DAMAGE button (which calls `Boss.takeDamage()`) continues to function correctly.
- [ ] **AC4 — EXPLODE still insta-kills:** The EXPLODE admin button continues to call `destroySelf()` and insta-kill the Boss.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- Must not break existing single-hit destruction for regular enemies (E1–E5).
- Changes should be surgical — only touch the collision handling path in `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()`.
- Must follow existing gym scene conventions.

## Existing state

`GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` (line 670–707) iterates over player bullets and enemy entities, and on collision calls `entity.destroySelf()` directly — bypassing `Boss.takeDamage()`. Regular enemies (E1–E5) use `destroySelf()` correctly. The Boss entity has a `takeDamage()` method at `src/entities/Boss.ts:652` that handles 4-phase health progression.

## Desired change

Modify `_handleCollisions()` to check if the collided entity supports `takeDamage()` (i.e., is a Boss), and if so, call `takeDamage()` instead of `destroySelf()`. For regular enemies, continue calling `destroySelf()`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Fix `_handleCollisions()` to delegate Boss hits to `takeDamage()`
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — Reference for `takeDamage()` and `destroySelf()`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — Add test: player bullets damage Boss through 4 phases
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — Verify regular enemies still die in 1 hit

## Related work

- **Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE)** — Parent implementation; Boss entity and gym scene created here.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — GDD §4.3 Boss Design.
- **Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model (AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR)** — Confirms only Boss is multi-hit.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — Accidentally changing collision for regular enemies:** If the fix is not careful, regular enemies may also start calling `takeDamage()`. Mitigation: type-check or interface-check to only call `takeDamage()` on Boss instances.
- **Risk — Existing tests may fail:** The Boss gym scene tests exercise DAMAGE/EXPLODE but not player bullets. New test coverage needed.
- **Assumption — Boss is the only entity with `takeDamage()`:** Regular enemies don't have this method; only Boss does. Verified by inspection.
- **Scope-creep risk:** This is a targeted bug fix. Do not extend to other scenes (e.g., main game levels) unless explicitly instructed.

## Clarifying questions & answers

_N/A — description was sufficiently detailed for intake auto-complete. No clarifying questions were asked._
